html:
Zenobia was the queen of Palmyra, a rich caravan city in the Syrian desert, who ruled from 267 for her young son and briefly built an empire in the Roman East.

Her husband Odaenathus had defended the Roman East against Persia and was murdered in 267. Zenobia took power and, while Rome was weak, her armies took Egypt and much of Anatolia around 270 and 271. She broke with Rome and named her son emperor.

The emperor Aurelian defeated her armies in 272 and took Palmyra. She was captured, and by most accounts lived out her life in Italy. She became a heroine in Syria and a figure of legend in Europe. Palmyra's Temple of Bel was blown up by the Islamic State in 2015. See also Palmyra.
sum: Zenobia was the queen of Palmyra, a rich caravan city in the Syrian desert, who ruled from 267 for her young son and briefly built an empire in the Roman East.
